key_insight: AtomWorld-Mirror learns a time-aware macro-step model that jumps between physically reachable atomic states, capturing critical evolution while skipping many low-impact micro-events.
engineering_relevance: This could dramatically accelerate long-horizon materials simulation for damage, diffusion, aging, and fracture without losing structural validity or time semantics.
method: Distills short atomistic micro-event segments into reusable latent macro-step dynamics
Predicts sparse structural edits plus accumulated physical time in a single transition
Uses local reachability, inventory conservation, and continuous-time consistency constraints
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation across five atomic systems, including Cu-rich RPV steel irradiation aging, Cu-Zr metallic glass, and Li$_3$N-based anti-perovskite solid electrolyte, with 10^3 to 10^4× speedup over event-by-event simulation.
watch_item: Macro-step inference must still reliably preserve rare-event physics and conservation constraints when extrapolating to unfamiliar materials or longer time horizons.
paper_title: AtomWorld-Mirror: Macro-Step World Modeling of Critical Evolution Backbones for Materials Dynamics
